options.content: Availability uses successful requests / (successful + service failures). Fast-success uses successful requests completed in <= 500 ms / all successful requests. A ratio is unknown when its request denominator is empty or the genuine gateway healthcheck heartbeat has expired. Check the separate heartbeat, target, and telemetry-loss panels; an unknown ratio is not 0% or 100%.

panels.title: Availability (5m)
panels.description: Unknown when the eligible request denominator is empty or the genuine gateway healthcheck heartbeat has expired (no event in 1m). No zero/one fallback is used.

panels.title: Fast-success (5m)
panels.description: Successful gateway requests completed in <= 500 ms divided by all successful in-scope requests. Unknown when the success denominator is empty or the genuine gateway healthcheck heartbeat has expired (no event in 1m).

panels.title: Gateway pipeline healthcheck count (1m)
panels.description: Only the genuine completed local GET /health/gateway event is counted; it is excluded from business SLI denominators. No data indicates heartbeat absence.

targets.expr:
sum(count_over_time(
  {service_name="gateway",deployment_environment_name="demo"} | json event="event" | __error__ = "" | event="gateway.healthcheck" | keep event
  [1m]
))

panels.title: Telemetry targets
panels.description: A missing gateway healthcheck is a telemetry gap only when target or loss evidence is unhealthy. Empty scrape data is not healthy.

panels.title: Gateway request logs
panels.description: Gateway JSON only. Request and trace IDs remain structured fields; the TraceID field has a Grafana link to Tempo.
